title: Jeremiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 7.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 7, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD
Stand in the gate of the LORD'S house
Amend your ways and your doings
Trust ye not in lying words
questions.correctAnswer: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD
questions.explanation: This is the first statement in the chapter, found in Jeremiah 7:1.

questions.question: What were the people of Judah instructed to do when they entered the gates?
options: Hear the word of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Hear the word of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:2 instructs the people to hear the word of the LORD as they enter the gates.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will do if the people amend their ways?
options: Cause them to dwell in this place
questions.correctAnswer: Cause them to dwell in this place
questions.explanation: According to Jeremiah 7:3, if they amend their ways, the LORD will cause them to dwell in this place.

questions.question: What should the people not trust in according to the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Lying words
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:4 warns the people not to trust in lying words.

questions.question: What is required for the people to avoid oppression?
options: Execute judgment between a man and his neighbour
questions.correctAnswer: Execute judgment between a man and his neighbour
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:5 states that they need to execute judgment between one another.

questions.question: Who are the vulnerable groups mentioned that the people should not oppress?
options: The stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
questions.correctAnswer: The stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:6 specifically mentions not oppressing the stranger, fatherless, and widow.

questions.question: What will happen if the people do not walk after other gods?
options: They will dwell in the land
questions.correctAnswer: They will dwell in the land
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:7 states that if they follow the commands, they will dwell in the land.

questions.question: What do the people trust in according to Jeremiah 7:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Lying words
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:8 points out that the people trust in lying words that cannot profit.

questions.question: Which of the following sins is mentioned in Jeremiah 7:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Stealing
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:9 lists stealing as one of the sins committed by the people.

questions.question: What do the people claim about their state in the house of the LORD?
options: They are delivered to do all these abominations
questions.correctAnswer: They are delivered to do all these abominations
questions.explanation: According to Jeremiah 7:10, they claim they are delivered to commit abominations.

questions.question: What has the house of the LORD become in the eyes of the people?
questions.correctAnswer: A den of robbers
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:11 states that the house has become a den of robbers in their eyes.

questions.question: What does the LORD instruct the people to do in Jeremiah 7:12?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:12 instructs the people to go to Shiloh to see what the LORD did for the wickedness of His people.

questions.question: The LORD set His name at Shiloh according to Jeremiah 7:12.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is confirmed in Jeremiah 7:12, where the LORD mentions setting His name at Shiloh.

questions.question: The people are encouraged to trust in the temple of the LORD according to Jeremiah 7:4.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:4 warns against trusting in the temple of the LORD, indicating that they should not.

questions.question: The people were told to oppress the fatherless according to Jeremiah 7:6.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:6 instructs the people not to oppress the fatherless, thus stating the opposite.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 7:13, what did the LORD say He did before the people failed to hear and answer?
options: I spake unto you, rising up early and speaking
I sent my angels to warn you
I gave you commandments on tablets of stone
questions.correctAnswer: I spake unto you, rising up early and speaking
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:13 states, 'And now, because ye have done all these works, saith the LORD, and I spake unto you, rising up early and speaking, but ye heard not; and I called you, but ye answered not;' showing God spoke to them early but they did not listen.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 7:14 promise will happen if the people continue to ignore God's warnings in Jeremiah 7:13?
options: God will do to this house as He did to Shiloh
God will bless their crops abundantly
God will give them peace forever
questions.correctAnswer: God will do to this house as He did to Shiloh
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:14 says, 'Therefore will I do unto this house, which is called by my name... as I have done to Shiloh,' indicating that disobedience will bring destruction similar to what happened at Shiloh, as a consequence of ignoring God's warnings in verse 13.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 7:16, what does God instruct Jeremiah regarding prayer for the people?
options: Do not pray or intercede for them, for He will not hear
Pray earnestly and continuously for their forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: Do not pray or intercede for them, for He will not hear
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:16 states, 'Therefore pray not thou for this people, neither lift up cry nor prayer for them, neither make intercession to me: for I will not hear thee,' showing God’s refusal to accept prayers for their forgiveness at that time.

questions.question: How do Jeremiah 7:18 and 7:19 together describe the people's actions and their effect on God?
options: The people worship the queen of heaven provoking God to anger and bringing confusion upon themselves
The people gather to pray and God blesses them abundantly
The people build altars to God and find favor in His sight
The people fast and repent, turning away from sin
questions.correctAnswer: The people worship the queen of heaven provoking God to anger and bringing confusion upon themselves
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:18 describes the people making cakes and pouring out drink offerings to the queen of heaven, provoking God’s anger as stated in 7:19, which adds that they provoke themselves to confusion, linking their idolatry to consequences.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 7:20 say will happen to man, beast, trees, and fruit of the ground as a result of God's anger?
options: God’s anger and fury will burn and not be quenched
God will bless them with rain and abundance
They will be protected from harm
They will be renewed and restored
questions.correctAnswer: God’s anger and fury will burn and not be quenched
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:20 states, 'Behold, mine anger and my fury shall be poured out upon this place, upon man, and upon beast, and upon the trees of the field, and upon the fruit of the ground; and it shall burn, and shall not be quenched,' indicating the severity of God's judgment.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 7:21, what does God say the people should do with their burnt offerings and sacrifices?
options: Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh
Offer them at the temple continually
Give them to the priests to distribute
Burn them as a pleasing aroma to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:21 commands, 'Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh,' implying that God rejects their offerings and they might as well eat the meat themselves, showing the futility of their worship without obedience.

questions.question: What did God declare to their fathers regarding burnt offerings and sacrifices in Jeremiah 7:22?
options: God did not command them concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices when bringing them out of Egypt
God commanded many burnt offerings and sacrifices
God required offerings to appease Him
God was pleased with constant sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: God did not command them concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices when bringing them out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:22 clarifies, 'For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices,' indicating that obedience was more important than ritual sacrifices.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 7:23, what was the primary command God gave to their fathers?
options: Obey my voice, and walk in all the ways I have commanded you
questions.correctAnswer: Obey my voice, and walk in all the ways I have commanded you
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:23 states, 'Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you,' emphasizing obedience over ritual sacrifice.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 7:24 say about the people's response to God's commands?
options: They did not listen nor incline their ear, but walked in the counsels of their evil heart
They eagerly obeyed and followed God's ways
They repented and returned to God
They built new temples to honor God
questions.correctAnswer: They did not listen nor incline their ear, but walked in the counsels of their evil heart
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:24 says, 'But they hearkened not, nor inclined their ear, but walked in the counsels and in the imagination of their evil heart,' showing their rebellion and disobedience despite God's commands.

questions.question: What practical lesson about prayer can be learned from Jeremiah 7:16 regarding interceding for others who persist in disobedience?
options: God may refuse to hear intercession if the people persist in sin
Prayer should always be persistent and never cease
Prayer should be done publicly only
questions.correctAnswer: God may refuse to hear intercession if the people persist in sin
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:16 shows that God tells Jeremiah not to pray for the people because He will not hear him, highlighting that persistent sin can lead to a time when prayer is not accepted.

questions.question: How does the example of Shiloh in Jeremiah 7:14 relate to God's judgment on the temple in Jerusalem?
options: God will bring destruction to the temple in Jerusalem just as He did to Shiloh due to wickedness
Shiloh will be rebuilt and blessed instead of Jerusalem
Shiloh was a model of perfect worship unlike Jerusalem
God will protect Jerusalem unlike Shiloh
questions.correctAnswer: God will bring destruction to the temple in Jerusalem just as He did to Shiloh due to wickedness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:14 references the destruction of Shiloh as a warning that God will similarly act against His house in Jerusalem because of the people's wickedness.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 7:19 suggest about the consequences of provoking God to anger through idolatry?
options: They provoke themselves to the confusion of their own faces
They will be blessed with prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: They provoke themselves to the confusion of their own faces
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:19 states, 'do they not provoke themselves to the confusion of their own faces?' indicating that idolatry leads to shame and confusion for the people themselves.

questions.question: What is the significance of walking 'backward, and not forward' in Jeremiah 7:24 in relation to spiritual progress?
options: It symbolizes regression and refusal to follow God’s ways
It shows careful reflection and caution
It indicates a new direction towards righteousness
It means advancing steadily in faith
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes regression and refusal to follow God’s ways
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:24 notes that the people 'went backward, and not forward,' meaning they regressed spiritually by ignoring God’s commands and following their own evil hearts.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 7:15 states that God will cast out the people 'as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim.'
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:15 clearly says, 'And I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim,' confirming the statement is true.

questions.question: True or False: According to Jeremiah 7:22, God commanded burnt offerings and sacrifices to their fathers when He brought them out of Egypt.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:22 explicitly states, 'For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them... concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices,' so the statement is false.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 7.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 7:25, who has God sent daily rising up early since the day the fathers came out of Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: All his servants the prophets
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:25 states God sent 'all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them'.

questions.question: Jeremiah 7:26 describes the people's response to God's prophets. How did they respond?
options: They hardened their neck and did worse than their fathers
They ignored the prophets but did not sin further
questions.correctAnswer: They hardened their neck and did worse than their fathers
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:26 says they 'hearkened not... but hardened their neck: they did worse than their fathers.'

questions.question: In Jeremiah 7:28, what has perished and is cut off from the mouths of the people?
questions.correctAnswer: Truth
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:28 says 'truth is perished, and is cut off from their mouth.'

questions.question: Jeremiah 7:29 commands Jerusalem to cut off what as a sign of lamentation?
questions.correctAnswer: Hair
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:29 says 'Cut off thine hair, O Jerusalem, and cast it away...'.

questions.question: What evil act is specifically mentioned in Jeremiah 7:31 as being done by the children of Judah?
options: Burning their sons and daughters in the fire
questions.correctAnswer: Burning their sons and daughters in the fire
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:31 says they 'have built the high places of Tophet... to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire.'

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 7:34, what will cease from the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem?
options: The voice of mirth and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and bride
The sound of the temple bells
questions.correctAnswer: The voice of mirth and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and bride
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:34 states 'I will cause to cease... the voice of mirth, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'nekar' (נכר) in Jeremiah 7:6 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Stranger
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 7:6, 'nekar' refers to the 'stranger', meaning a foreigner or sojourner, emphasizing protection for outsiders.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Jeremiah 7:28-29 where two contrasting states are presented in parallel?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:28-29 uses parallelism by juxtaposing the nation's disobedience and the lamentation commanded as consequences.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of false trust in the temple as in Jeremiah 7:4-11?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 29:13
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:13 echoes the theme of hollow worship and misplaced trust in the temple, similar to Jeremiah 7:4-11.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the warning about the temple being made a 'den of robbers' as in Jeremiah 7:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 21:13
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:13 quotes Jesus calling the temple a 'den of robbers', directly fulfilling Jeremiah 7:11.

questions.question: What immediately precedes Jeremiah 7:25 which speaks about God sending prophets from Egypt to that day?
options: A command to obey God's voice and walk in His ways
A description of the high places of Tophet
A lamentation about Jerusalem's destroyed joy
A warning to cut off hair as a sign of mourning
questions.correctAnswer: A command to obey God's voice and walk in His ways
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:24 immediately precedes 7:25 and commands obedience to God's voice and walking in His ways.

questions.question: Jeremiah 7:31 condemns the practice of child sacrifice. What cultural and historical context underlies this practice?
options: Influence of Canaanite religion and worship of Molech
questions.correctAnswer: Influence of Canaanite religion and worship of Molech
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:31 condemns burning children in the fire, linked historically to Canaanite worship of Molech in the valley of Hinnom.

questions.question: How does the description of Tophet in Jeremiah 7:32 use typology to foreshadow future judgment?
options: Changing its name to 'valley of slaughter' symbolizes complete destruction
It predicts a future temple renovation
It promises restoration of Israel's fortunes
It allegorizes the resurrection of the dead
questions.correctAnswer: Changing its name to 'valley of slaughter' symbolizes complete destruction
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:32 uses the renaming of Tophet as typology to foreshadow total judgment and desolation.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 7:27 states that Jeremiah's words will be hearkened to and answered by the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:27 states that though Jeremiah shall speak, 'they will not hearken to thee... they will not answer thee.'

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 7:29 commands Jerusalem to take up a lamentation because the LORD has rejected and forsaken the generation of his wrath.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:29 commands Jerusalem to lament because 'the LORD hath rejected and forsaken the generation of his wrath.'

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 7:3 teach about God's relationship with obedience and dwelling?
options: God promises eternal life regardless of conduct
God will cause His people to dwell in the land if they amend their ways and doings
God's presence is guaranteed in the temple without conditions
God's favor is based solely on ritual sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: God will cause His people to dwell in the land if they amend their ways and doings
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:3 teaches that God promises to cause the people to dwell in the land if they amend their ways and doings, indicating conditional covenantal blessing based on obedience.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment and social ethics is taught in Jeremiah 7:5?
options: Judgment between man and neighbor is irrelevant to God's covenant
Judgment must be executed thoroughly between neighbors as part of covenantal obedience
God accepts superficial justice without concern for neighbors
Social ethics have no bearing on spiritual worship
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment must be executed thoroughly between neighbors as part of covenantal obedience
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:5 emphasizes that thorough execution of judgment between man and neighbor is essential to covenantal obedience, linking social justice to divine blessing.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of true worship does Jeremiah 7:22-23 convey?
options: God commands burnt offerings and sacrifices above obedience
True worship is obedience to God's voice and walking in His ways
Ritual sacrifices are the sole requirement for being God's people
Obedience is irrelevant if sacrifices are offered
questions.correctAnswer: True worship is obedience to God's voice and walking in His ways
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:22-23 teaches that God did not command burnt offerings or sacrifices but rather obedience to His voice and walking in His ways as the true form of worship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 7:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:11 demonstrates God's omniscience as He declares that He has seen the temple become a den of robbers, showing His all-knowing awareness of human actions.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by God's repeated sending of prophets in Jeremiah 7:25?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:25 highlights God's mercy in His persistent sending of prophets to call the people to repentance despite their disobedience.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 7:12 prepare for the theme of judgment found later in the Old Testament?
options: It predicts the final restoration of Israel
It recalls the destruction of Shiloh as a precedent for judgment
It promises immediate forgiveness without consequences
It denies any connection between past and present judgments
questions.correctAnswer: It recalls the destruction of Shiloh as a precedent for judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:12 connects the current judgment to the historical judgment on Shiloh, preparing the reader for the theme of covenantal consequences in later scripture.

questions.question: In what way does Jeremiah 7:31 relate to the broader biblical narrative of idolatry and child sacrifice?
options: It endorses child sacrifice as a legitimate worship practice
It condemns child sacrifice as an abomination not commanded by God
It is silent on the morality of child sacrifice
It suggests child sacrifice was commanded by God
questions.correctAnswer: It condemns child sacrifice as an abomination not commanded by God
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:31 clearly condemns the building of high places for child sacrifice, emphasizing that this was never commanded or in God's heart, connecting to the biblical rejection of idolatrous practices.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 7:4 and 7:8 teach about the danger of misplaced trust?
options: Trusting in the temple's name alone is sufficient for salvation
Lying words and misplaced trust in the temple cannot profit
Faith is irrelevant to God's covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: Lying words and misplaced trust in the temple cannot profit
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:4 and 7:8 together emphasize that trusting in the temple's name or lying words is futile, highlighting that true trust must be grounded in obedience and truth.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine judgment and human rebellion is taught in Jeremiah 7:13 and 7:14?
options: Persistent disobedience despite prophetic warning results in judgment on the temple and land
Judgment is delayed indefinitely regardless of rebellion
Prophets have no role in warning the people
questions.correctAnswer: Persistent disobedience despite prophetic warning results in judgment on the temple and land
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:13 and 7:14 teach that despite God's early and repeated warnings through prophets, the people's continued disobedience leads to judgment on the temple and the land.

questions.question: What theological synthesis do Jeremiah 7:18 and 7:19 reveal about idolatry and its consequences?
options: Idolatry provokes God to anger but benefits the people
Idolatry provokes God to anger and leads to the people's shame
Idolatry is overlooked by God if done collectively
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry provokes God to anger and leads to the people's shame
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:18-19 shows that idolatry provokes God's anger and simultaneously brings confusion and shame upon the people themselves, revealing the spiritual and social consequences of such sin.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Jeremiah 7:16-17 teaches that prayer is useless and God is unmerciful. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God refuses to hear prayers because the people persist in evil
God never listens to any prayers under any circumstances
Prayer can change God's mind regardless of sin
God is indifferent to human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God refuses to hear prayers because the people persist in evil
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:16-17 indicates that God will not hear Jeremiah's intercession because the people continue in their sins, emphasizing the seriousness of persistent rebellion rather than God's total unwillingness to listen.

questions.question: What doctrine about human depravity and truth is taught in Jeremiah 7:28?
options: The nation embraces truth and correction
The nation rejects God's voice and correction, and truth has perished from their mouth
The nation is eager to repent and receive correction
Truth is preserved among the people despite rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: The nation rejects God's voice and correction, and truth has perished from their mouth
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:28 describes the nation as one that does not obey God nor receive correction, with truth perished and cut off from their mouth, illustrating deep human depravity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially evident in Jeremiah 7:20 with the pouring out of God's anger and fury?
questions.correctAnswer: Wrath
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:20 explicitly reveals God's wrath as His anger and fury are poured out upon the land and people, demonstrating the just response to persistent sin.

questions.question: How do Jeremiah 7:30-31 and 7:34 together teach about the consequences of idolatry on community and worship life?
options: Idolatry leads to the pollution of the temple and eventual desolation of the land
Idolatry has no lasting effect on worship or community life
Idolatry results in immediate national blessing
Idolatry is secretly approved by God
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry leads to the pollution of the temple and eventual desolation of the land
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:30-31 show idolatry polluting the temple, while 7:34 predicts desolation and cessation of joy in the land, demonstrating the severe communal consequences of idolatry.

questions.question: What theological insight about the covenant relationship is given in Jeremiah 7:6?
options: Oppression of the stranger, fatherless, and widow is compatible with the covenant
Covenant obedience includes justice and mercy toward the stranger, fatherless, and widow
Ritual worship alone secures the covenant
God ignores social injustice in the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant obedience includes justice and mercy toward the stranger, fatherless, and widow
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:6 teaches that covenant obedience requires not oppressing the stranger, fatherless, and widow, integrating social justice as a vital part of faithfulness to God.
